title: Nine-Volt
subject: a smoke alarm chirping for a new battery at three in the morning on a ceiling you cannot reach
caption: Atmospheric alt-metal with metalcore breakdowns. A soft felt-piano intro under a clean male voice; drop-tuned seven-string guitars in drop A playing palm-muted djent chugs locked to the kick; live acoustic drums with a triggered kick, moving between half-time breakdowns and double-kick runs; an 808 sub drop under each breakdown; a low choir pad behind the choruses. Close and dry in the piano sections, wide and roomy in the choruses, guitars and kick forward. Male voice, a clean high tenor that reaches into falsetto, switching to screamed harsh vocals in the second verse and the breakdown. 140 BPM with half-time breakdowns, C-sharp minor. Sleep-deprived rage, played completely straight. No pop-punk skate beat, no rap verse, no autotune, no standard-tuned indie guitars, no trap hi-hats.
lyrics:
[Intro - soft felt piano, one high electronic chirp every few bars]

[Verse 1 - clean, close]
Three-oh-eight and the hallway chirps again
One short note, then forty seconds of nothing
I stand in the dark in my socks and I wait for it
It waits for me. It's better at waiting.

[Pre-Chorus]
The ceiling's eleven feet
The ladder's at my brother's

[Chorus - full band, half-time]
Nine-volt, nine-volt
You want a battery, I want my life back
I'm on a kitchen chair on top of the dining table
And I still can't reach you

[Verse 2 - screamed]
I took a broom to it at four
Now it's not chirping, it's screaming
Every light on the street comes on
Mrs Patel's at her gate in a dressing gown

[Chorus - full band, half-time]
Nine-volt, nine-volt
You want a battery, I want my life back
Two firemen in my hallway at half past four
And the tall one just reaches up

[Bridge - half-time breakdown, 808 drop, screamed]
He didn't even stand on his toes
He didn't even stand on his toes

[Outro - piano alone, no chirp]
Five-oh-two. It's quiet.
Now I can't sleep without it.
